drafts.body: Thanks for the follow-up, and I'm sorry you've been chasing this for four days. You're right that it's on our side — we've confirmed a checkout failure affecting high-value orders across a number of accounts, and it lines up with a recent deploy on our end. It's escalated to engineering now as a top priority, though I don't have a fix timeline I can give you yet. I've noted the ~$18k in abandoned carts on your ticket so it's part of the record when we review impact — I'll update you as soon as engineering has something concrete.

Thanks for the detail on the three failures (€1,250, €1,900 and €4,100) and for testing with the €40 order — that contrast is exactly what we needed. We've confirmed a problem affecting checkout on higher-value orders across multiple accounts, and it correlates with a recent deploy on our side. Engineering is investigating now; no fix has shipped yet, so I can't give you a firm time. Smaller orders should keep processing normally in the meantime, and I'll come back to you as soon as I have news.

Your customers' banks are right — no charge attempt is reaching them, because the order is failing on our side before it gets that far. So the "decline" message is misleading; it isn't a card problem. We've confirmed this affects higher-value orders like the $1,600 and $2,050 ones you saw, it's tied to a recent deploy, and engineering is on it now. No fix is out yet, but I'll let you know as soon as that changes.

Thanks for the trace — that's genuinely useful. We've confirmed POST /v2/transactions is returning 500s on higher-value requests, matching your observation that only four-figure-plus orders are affected, and it correlates with a deploy we made Tuesday afternoon. It's escalated to engineering and under active investigation; nothing has shipped yet, so I can't give you a fix time. I'll follow up here with whatever engineering finds.

Treating this as P1 — you're one of 12 accounts hitting the same thing, and it's already escalated to engineering. We've confirmed that high-value carts, including five-figure ones like your quarterly restocks, fail at checkout, and it correlates with a recent deploy on our side rather than anything browser-specific (which matches your Chrome and Edge results). No fix has shipped yet, so I won't guess at a time. I'll update you directly as engineering makes progress.

Thanks for reporting this, and bad timing with high season. We've confirmed a checkout failure affecting higher-value orders — bookings over €1,000 in your case — across several accounts, and it's tied to a recent deploy on our side, not to Safari or Firefox specifically. Engineering is investigating now; there's no fix out yet, so I can't promise a date. Smaller bookings should continue to go through while we work on it, and I'll update you as soon as I hear more.

Sorry you lost that sale — the white screen your shopper hit is a real bug on our side, not anything she did wrong. We've confirmed that checkout is failing on higher-value orders across a number of accounts, and it lines up with a recent deploy we made. Engineering is investigating now; no fix has gone out yet, so I don't have a date to give you. If you can tell me roughly what her cart total was, that helps confirm it's the same issue, and I'll update you when there's news.

Thanks for the console detail — the 30-second timeout on /v2/transactions matches what we're seeing elsewhere. We've confirmed that requests for higher-value orders, like your distributor orders above ¥150,000, are failing while smaller consumer orders go through, and it correlates with a recent deploy on our side. It's escalated to engineering and under investigation; nothing has shipped yet, so I can't give you a fix time. I'll follow up here as soon as engineering has something.

Thanks for testing the 5-seat purchase — that comparison confirms what we suspected. We've identified a problem where higher-value orders fail at the final checkout step, which is why the 40+ seat licences hang while small purchases complete, and it correlates with a recent deploy on our side. Engineering is investigating now; no fix has shipped yet, so I can't give you a date. I'll update you as soon as there's progress.

Thanks for flagging this — both of those failed orders being over $1,000 fits a problem we've already confirmed. Checkout is failing on higher-value orders across a number of accounts, and it correlates with a recent deploy on our side, so it's nothing to do with your setup. Engineering is investigating now, but no fix has shipped yet, so I can't give you a time. If it helps with the customers messaging you, you can tell them it's a temporary problem with the payment step that we're working on.

Yes — it's a problem on our side, and you're not the only one seeing it. Checkout is failing on higher-value orders, which fits the two big landscaping quotes that couldn't be completed this morning, and it correlates with a recent deploy we made. Engineering has it and is investigating; no fix has shipped yet, so I can't promise a date. Smaller orders should still go through, and I'll let you know as soon as there's an update.

The endless spinner on that $1,300 patio set is a bug on our end — the payment request never comes back, so the page just keeps waiting. We've confirmed this affects higher-value orders across several accounts and it isn't browser-related, which matches you seeing it in both Chrome and Safari. It correlates with a recent deploy and is now with engineering; no fix has shipped yet, so I can't give you a date. Cheaper items should keep working, and I'll update you when I hear more.
